name: Reclaim the City
author: Multiverse Video editors
description: Learn how people redesign the systems that shape daily life.

items.note: A clear introduction to housing co-ops: how residents own and run their buildings together, and why it keeps rents down.
Three minutes presenting DAIR's report on Amazon delivery drivers: how workplace surveillance tech is used to cut pay and hide responsibility.
The story of B4RN, a community-built fibre network in rural England that has connected over 7,000 homes through joint action, with captions.
From Battlemesh v15: how the COWMesh community network brought connectivity to a rural area in India, built and run by locals.
Waag Futurelab's yearly State of the Internet lecture, 2026 edition, given in English by Fieke Jansen with captions.
A practical guide to tenant rights for first-time renters in Montreal: rent increases, repairs, and what landlords can and can't do.
The Bonfire project on federated digital spaces built for mutual aid networks, as an alternative to running them on corporate group chats.
A FOSS4G talk on interactive open-source tools for visualizing climate risk, used in disaster-reduction programmes.
A four-minute APC short on where digital rights and environmental justice meet, with captions.
New Design Congress on the 'para-real': how decentralised networks of care form when official systems fail people.
An honest DIY test: can one solar panel on a shed roof run a home server rack, or does it just cost money?
A short documentary on co-creating climate resilience plans between residents and city administration over eight weeks, with captions.
An unedited interview with Move Minnesota's MJ Carpio on how transit advocates actually win changes in their city.
